title: Let the last mistake go
header_line: My analysis of one book on neuro-linguistic programming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What do you do with the bad shot you just played?
A student said: it is about deleting the last shot from your mind. If you hit eight bad shots in a row, you walk up to the ninth and forget the last eight and focus on the shot.
I said that if you have had eight bad shots and you are not focused on the process and the adjustments, you let them become an abstraction: I am having a bad day, I am losing.

groups.heading: A bunker is a place to get out of

lines.text: I said that I loved a player's remark: I am in the bunker, I have to hit out of the bunker, and that it is like being in a big loss in business: you just have to get out of it.
A student said that if he lets his body react to bad thoughts during mistakes, the body follows along.

I said that there are different techniques: the cube you put the thought in and throw away, a river flowing by, a waterfall. The book gives a practice with a visualization to bring up a voice from a negative moment.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the last mistake you replay.
Write the process step for the next one.
Write the image you will use: a cube, a river or a waterfall.

check.q: What did a student say to delete?
What did I say eight bad shots can become?
choices: An abstraction like I am losing
A cube, a river, a waterfall
A map, a phone, a clock
A mountain, a sun, a star

recap: Delete the last shot. Use an image. Focus on the process.
